summary: Setup carried over from run 1 unchanged (era, opening situation, System origin; run-1 rolls roll_t0_1..3, not re-rolled). Tables and results in hidden/GM_LEDGER.md.
The System's seed: a shard of a Sith-alchemical tally holocron, woken on Dovrenn.
Garrick Tolliver unearthed the shard in Silo Three. Its first awards fell on the drover-dogs; the pack is altered, mimics voices heard over the comm, alpha Biscuit. Six settlers missing.
Warden Tolliver believes the thing listens to the comm and learns whom to call back as.
The pack hunts after dusk. Next review: one hour after dusk, Day 1.

Ruddick, Charisma (Persuasion) +4, DC 15 (convictions: schedule and self-preservation; the ask names no number and offers him nothing on safety; Aero is a Jedi Knight asking, not someone with authority to order him):
- 20+: he agrees to stay on the ground until Aero calls him from the settlement, on his own terms: ramp up and sealed, engines warm, and he lifts the moment anything comes at the shuttle.
- 15-19: he agrees to a fixed extension: thirty more minutes from now, ramp up once Aero is off it, then he lifts; Aero must call in when he reaches the settlement.
- 10-14: he does not move the schedule; he grants only that he will lift late enough for Aero to reach the settlement's comm and call him back on a later run if needed (no promise of when); the clock stays at about six minutes.
- under 10: he refuses flatly, keeps the clock, and says he raises the ramp in two minutes whether Aero is aboard or not.
Wick, at the ramp foot, hearing Aero say he has a way in (d6): 1-3 stays where he is, listening, eyes on the trees; 4-5 turns and looks up the ramp at Aero, waiting to hear Ruddick's answer; 6 calls up: 'I can take you. I know the track in the dark.'
Pack during the exchange (d6; Aero and Wick stay on the open, lit field side, so none of the four rises in any case, tactic 1-2): 1-3 all silent, nothing moves; 4-5 the woman's voice calls again from under the trees, the same words; 6 from under the trees a voice replays a line from the earlier comm exchange verbatim (evt_0044: Ruddick's 'Ruddick. Go ahead, Knight. I can see your blade at the fence. You've got about eight minutes.').

Wick's response to "Wick, I know whose voice you think that is. Don't go to it like this. Stay with me and we look for her the right way." (d6; from his convictions: no one left behind; the intention read in evt_0080; the line names his fear and offers him a way; the track they take runs toward the voice). In no result does he leave the track or Aero's reach this turn:
- 1: no answer; jaw set; he leads up the track a step ahead, eyes on the treeline the whole way.
- 2-3: a long breath, then "Okay." He leads up the track a step ahead, within reach. The pull toward the voice is still visible in how he walks.
- 4-5: "The right way goes where she's calling from." He leads up the track a step ahead, within reach.
- 6: he turns his head: "You'll go with me? To her? Not just to the settlement?" and waits a beat for an answer before leading on, within reach.

Shuttle sensors (hidden fact, undecided until now; Ruddick's courier shuttle, a Republic Courier Corps light courier; his convictions: self-preservation makes him willing to look; no roll for willingness). What the shuttle can resolve from the ground of warm bodies lying in long grass about 300 ft away in full dark (d6):
- 1-2: nothing useful. Its sensor suite is built for traffic, approach and docking; at ground level the grass and the fence return clutter. The cockpit view is black. No long-range sensor reads ground contacts through grass.
- 3-4: the approach camera's thermal channel shows warm smudges in the grass outside the fence near the corner: more than one, low to the ground, each about the size of a man lying down. No count at that range. Nothing further out.
- 5-6: a clean thermal read: four warm contacts in the grass near the corner, low and still, and a fifth further out to the north along the treeline. Sizes as 3-4.
Ruddick reports what he sees plainly. His plan (evt_0066) is unchanged: nothing is coming at the shuttle.

- below their total: nothing but the hiss of the comm and Wick's breathing; whatever is out there is lying still.
- equal or above: breathing, slow and deep, low to the ground beyond the rails, more than one; the nearest roughly 30 ft north of the corner, close to where the track runs; at least one more to the west along the fence.
- 5 or more above: as above, and he can separate four of them: two west along the fence line (about 40-60 ft) and two north of the corner near the track (about 30-40 ft); the breathing of animals heavier than a man.

details.tables:
Tables fixed before rolling for amw5xodjw124w1h

Interpretation (GM ruling). Out of combat: no action economy, beats in sequence. The structured part passed the validator, but its preview order (move 15 ft, then take hold of Wick 5 ft away) would put Wick out of reach; the free text makes the intent clear (keep Wick, get off the track, go on quietly). Order used: (1) the line to Wick, aloud; the comm channel is open, so it also goes out over it; (2) the blade goes dark; Aero keeps the hilt in his right hand, thumb on the activator; (3) Aero takes hold of Wick; (4) together they step off the ruts about 15 ft to the right onto the cropped pasture; (5) they go on north toward the settlement across the pasture, about 15 ft east of the ruts and parallel to them, at a sneaking pace, for about 30 ft; the beat ends there, at the pack's response (the next decision point). The route to the settlement is the cart track north past the treeline (Wick, evt_0050; up_track option).
Hands: the right hand holds the dark hilt (thumb on the activator, as declared); the left hand still holds the drawn blaster (not holstered; nothing declared). Taking hold of Wick therefore uses the blaster hand: the back of that hand and wrist against his shoulder, the muzzle down, steering him, not a grip. A real grip needs a free hand. This is stated in the next turn context.

Wick's response (d6; convictions: no one left behind; the intention leaning toward the voice (evt_0080); this line grants that his mother may be alive and denies only that the voice is her; the blade going dark; a hand at his shoulder steering him off the track). In no result does he break from Aero this turn: the voice has not called again, he is under Aero's hand, and the move is short.
- 1: no answer; he lets himself be steered off the ruts but walks stiff, head turned to the trees, the lantern lit and lifted toward them.
- 2-3: "You don't know that." Low, shaking. He comes with the hand; the lantern stays lit, held low at his knee.
- 4-5: a long silence; he comes; when the blade goes out he looks at the lantern and slides its shutter most of the way closed: a dim slit of glow at his knee.
- 6: a whisper: "Then where is she?" He comes, and slides the lantern's shutter fully closed: full dark.
(World fact, GM placement: Wick's lantern is an ordinary hooded farm lantern with a slide shutter.)

Going unseen (the pack: darkvision 60 ft, keen hearing and smell, Perception +4, advantage by sound or smell; PACK_PROFILE). Positions at the start (evt_0103): two dogs behind, 25-40 ft; two to the left, 15-30 ft; the voice-dog ~90 ft ahead.
- Wick 1-3 (lantern lit): no Stealth roll. A lit lantern on open, cropped pasture shows the pair to anything watching; going quietly does not hide them. The pack keeps them exactly.
- Wick 4-5 (dim slit): group Stealth, Aero 1d20+3 and Wick 1d20+2 (Wick: provisional NPC value, Dex +2, no proficiency), both at disadvantage (the glow at knee height on open ground), against one pack Perception roll 1d20+4 with advantage (sound and smell), rolled first. The group succeeds if at least one of the two meets or beats it.
- Wick 6 (dark): the same group Stealth without disadvantage.
Success = the pack loses their exact place for now (it knows the area, not the spot). Failure = the pack keeps them.

Pack response (d6). Tactic 1-2 of PACK_PROFILE: lure, isolate; they do not rush a pair in the open; the pair has left the grass edge for open pasture and has not come to the lure. No dog attacks this turn in any result. The voice-dog replays only recordings it heard: Aero's new line was spoken aloud in still air with the channel open, about 90 ft from it (keen hearing), so it is available to it.
If the pack keeps them:
- 1-2: the four move up through the long grass along the west side of the track, keeping pace with the pair, staying in the grass. The voice is silent.
- 3-4: as 1-2, and the woman's voice calls again from under the trees, the same words and breaths.
- 5: as 1-2, and from under the trees Aero's own voice replays the line he just spoke, verbatim: "Wick, if that thing can wear my voice, it can wear hers. I'm not saying she's gone. I'm saying that isn't her."
- 6: the two dogs behind come out of the grass onto the pasture behind the pair, low, and fan wide, one to the south and one to the south-east, about 40 ft back, then stop: drover-work, closing the way back and pressing the pair north toward the trees; the two on the left keep pace in the grass. No voice. They do not close further this turn.
If the pack loses them:
- 1-3: the four rise in the grass and cast about, heads up, scenting, spreading along the west side of the track; none comes onto the pasture. The voice is silent.
- 4-5: as 1-3, and Aero's own voice replays the line he just spoke, verbatim, from under the trees (calling for an answer).
- 6: as 1-3, and the woman's voice calls again, the same words.
For every result where dogs move in the grass: one group Stealth for the moving dogs, 1d20+2, against Aero's passive Perception 14 (by sound): 14 or less, he hears movement in the grass to his left and behind (and, if the pack lost them, that it is spreading and searching rather than pacing); 15+, he hears nothing. The two that come out onto the pasture in result 6 are seen in the lantern light if it is lit or dim, and heard (no roll: open stubble, deliberately) if it is dark.

Wick when a voice calls (no roll): he flinches and stops, his head snapping to it; under Aero's hand he does not pull away this turn. What he does next is decided next turn from Aero's response and his convictions.
Time: about two minutes; about 24 minutes left on Ruddick's clock. The pack review one hour after dusk (evt_0005) is not yet reached. Ruddick hears the line over the channel; no response from him this turn (his plan evt_0066 unchanged).
Positions at the end: Aero and Wick on the pasture about 15 ft east of the ruts and about 90 ft north of the gap; the treeline about 60 ft ahead; the voice-dog under the trees near the track, about 60 ft ahead and a little to the left.

The boy's been out there long enough."; then, having heard the man call Wick "Hallan's boy" (evt_0192), Aero asks "Is Hallan in there?"; then "Wick is not convinced that his mother isn't in the woods with... whatever that is." The player gave these words in quotes, so they are quoted. The comm channel is open, so all of it also goes out over it. (2) Aero deactivates the indigo blade (free object interaction; state flag saber_ignited removed). The only light outside the door is now Wick's open lantern, held up toward the lane; the hall's yellow light comes through the gap. (3) Aero looks solemnly at Wick and gestures to be let in: the body language of the appeal, part of the Persuasion action. (4) The man at the door answers (Persuasion, below). (5) Aero stays at the door (hold). The narration stops when the man has answered: whether and how Aero goes in is his decision.
"Hallan": in the man's words, "Hallan's boy" names the boy's family. Wick's mother Daria (GM_LEDGER: among the six missing) is a Hallan; the man knows this. Whether Wick has a father, and where, is not established and stays undecided; the man does not raise it in any result.
Persuasion: Charisma (Persuasion) +4 (sheet), normal mode. No rule grants advantage; the blade going out is part of the approach and is accounted for in the DC. DC 15 (hidden): he knows Wick by name and the boy is plainly himself; against it, nobody in the hall has answered him (evt_0192), and the hall believes anything can talk out there. Result bands:
- 15 or more: he answers the question, low: "Daria. Daria Hallan. His mam. She's not in here." His eyes go to the boy's back and stay there a moment. Then he lets the rifle muzzle drop toward the floor, closes the door enough to slip the chain, and opens it wide enough for two to pass, stepping back into the hall: "In. Quick." The doorway stands open; neither Aero nor Wick has gone in.
- 10 to 14: he answers the question the same way ("Daria. Daria Hallan. His mam. She's not in here."), but the chain stays: "It's not my door to open." Over his shoulder, into the hall: "Get the Warden." He stays at the gap, rifle low. Nobody arrives before the narration stops.
- 9 or less: he does not answer the question. His eyes go to Wick: "Wick. Come here, son. Just you. He waits." The chain stays on. Wick does not move or answer, no roll: his conviction is that no one is left behind (GM_LEDGER), and he is keeping watch as Aero asked (evt_0190).
Wick's reaction to hearing Aero tell the man about his mother (d6, independent of the Persuasion result; Wick keeps facing the lane with the lantern up, beside Aero, within reach, in every result):
- 1-3: he says nothing; his shoulder goes rigid against Aero's arm.
- 4-5: without turning, quietly: "She's not dead."
- 6: he turns his head and looks at Aero, then at the man in the gap, then back up the lane; he says nothing.
Hearing: about a minute passes. The five dogs are about 2,000 ft back in the strip of trees (evt_0193); Biscuit's group is not within about 200 ft of the lane (evt_0180); the pack review one hour after dusk (evt_0005) is not reached. No dog is in hearing; no pack roll. Ruddick hears all three lines over the channel; none is addressed to him; he says nothing (plan evt_0066, no roll). Who inside heard the comm line, and the Warden's belief (evt_0004), stay undecided/unrevealed.
Time: about a minute. About 11 minutes remain on Ruddick's clock.

Tables fixed before rolling for amw744lxdmsdlx3

Interpretation (GM ruling). Out of combat: beats in the validator's preview order, with the unmapped free text placed as the content of the declared call. (1) Speech, aloud at the chained door, the chosen line: "My pilot lifts in about eleven minutes, with or without me. Tell the Warden that." The comm channel is open, so it also goes out over it. (2) The call_ruddick action: the unmapped free text is what Aero says to Ruddick over the open channel. It is addressed by name and given as direct speech, so it is quoted. The composer cut it off at its character limit mid-word ("tria"); the only reading of "have you on tria" is "have you on trial", so that one word is completed and nothing is added: "Ruddick, can you search for a spot to land over here or hover at least? I can grapple up with some synthrope if I must. But if you leave, so help me, at first light I will have you on trial." Aero carries 50 ft of syntherope (sheet inventory); it is mentioned, not used. (3) Aero stays at the door (hold). (4) Ruddick answers (Persuasion, below). (5) Wick and the door answer (tables below). The narration stops there: what Aero does next is his decision.
Skill: one check for the call. The declared option is Persuasion (argue for more time); the request leads and the threat is the closing leverage, so it is one Charisma (Persuasion) +4 check, and the threat is weighed in the DC, not rolled separately. Normal mode, consistent with the earlier call to Ruddick (roll_t5_14): no rule grants advantage; the mantle's diplomacy advantage needs recognized Jedi status to materially assist, and Ruddick already acted on that status when he granted the extension (evt_0066); it is not what moves him now.
DC 17 (hidden). Ruddick's convictions: schedule and self-preservation (GM_LEDGER). The ask is larger than the extension (DC 15): move the shuttle at night to ground he has not seen, over a settlement where something talks in other people's voices, with no sensor that resolves ground contacts (evt_0098). The threat cuts both ways: a Jedi's complaint is a real risk to a Courier Corps career (self-preservation), and it is also a threat. Result bands:
- 22 or more: "...Copy. Find me open ground near you, flat, nothing on it, and light it. Call it when you're standing on it. I'll put her down, ramp stays shut until you're at it, and I lift the moment anything comes at her." He will come when called, inside the remaining clock. The clock is otherwise unchanged.
- 17 to 21: "I'm not putting her down blind in a farmyard. I'll hover. You call it, you name the open ground, I come over low, one pass, ramp down. One minute. You'd better be able to climb." He will come when called, inside the remaining clock (about 10 minutes); he will not land.
- 12 to 16: "Negative. I'm not putting her down blind on a farm lane at night, and I'm not hanging her over one either." To the threat: "Log it, Knight. I'll log mine." The clock stands: about 10 minutes, then he lifts from the silos field.
- 11 or less: "You want it on the record? Put this on it." The clock is cut: he lifts in five minutes from now, from where he is.
Ruddick's new plan (any band) is committed as npc_plan, superseding evt_0066 only where it changes it; the 'lifts sooner if something comes at the shuttle' clause stands in every band.
Wick, beside Aero, hearing both lines (d6; he keeps facing up the lane with the lantern raised, within reach, in every result; his conviction is that no one is left behind; his mother is missing):
- 1-4: he says nothing. The lantern doesn't move.
- 5-6: without turning, low: "You're going back to the ship."
The door (d6; the man sent for the Warden a minute ago, evt_0203; Warden Marga Tolliver: distrusts Jedi, believes late help is no help; nothing hidden is revealed and nobody comes out in any result; the chain stays on in every result):
- 1-2: no one comes. The man repeats it over his shoulder into the hall, flat: "Says his pilot lifts in eleven minutes." No answer that Aero hears. He stays at the gap.
- 3-4: footsteps inside, coming. The man looks back, says "Warden's coming," and stays at the gap. No one else reaches it before the narration stops.
- 5-6: the man steps aside from the gap; a woman about sixty, grey-haired, straight-backed, takes his place behind the chain and looks at Aero, at the dead hilt, at Wick's back. "You're late, Jedi." The chain stays on. She waits.
Hearing: about a minute passes. The five dogs are about 2,000 ft back in the strip of trees; Biscuit's group not within about 200 ft of the lane (evt_0204); pack review (evt_0005) not reached. No dog is in hearing of either line or of Ruddick's answer from the collar speaker; no pack roll. Ruddick's answer from the collar speaker is heard by Wick and by whoever is at the gap.
Time: about a minute. About 10 minutes remain on Ruddick's clock unless his answer changes it.

summary: Ruddick's plan (table evt_0209, 11-or-less band, roll 7): he will not land near the settlement or hover; the clock is cut: he lifts in five minutes from this exchange, from where he is on the field by the silos track, ramp sealed; sooner if anything comes at the shuttle. Supersedes the timing in evt_0066.
